## Make-up of the 1st Midterm: Types, types, types…

A new developer implemented the functionality needed to determine, at the moment of importing a Customer (method `importCustomer` of `CustomerImporter`), whether the identification type is DNI or CUIT, with their corresponding validations.

He did the same at the moment of importing an Address (method `importAddress` of `CustomerImporter`), with the goal of being able to tell the old postal code (only 4 digits, e.g. 1636) from the new postal code (e.g. B1336BBE).

Because of these document types and postal code types, he added protocol in `Customer` and `Address` to tell them apart.

Luckily there are tests for everything new. However, it seems he was unaware of good design practices and used IF in places where he could have used polymorphism, and he also left quite a lot of repeated code.

Your task is to remove the IFs and the repeated code you consider necessary in order to leave a good design. Any design and implementation change you consider necessary can be made, but the tests have to be kept as they are.

Use the code already loaded in the category `CustomerImporter-Recu-1er-Parcial` as the starting point.

Work in the Cuis Smalltalk image this directory gives you access to; it is the only place your work is read from, and there is no interactive access to it. I removed the IFs that checked the ID type and zip code type, and replaced them with classes. All 29 tests pass, and I didn't change any of them. They also all pass when run against the persistent customer system (`PersistentCustomerSystem`); I rolled the image back after that run so the environment setting wasn't saved.

## New classes
**`ValidatedValue`** is a new abstract class for values that are checked when they are created.
- `from: aString` checks the value with `isValid:`. If the check fails, it raises the error from `invalidErrorDescription`; otherwise it creates the object.
- Subclasses only define those two methods. The "all digits" check (`isAllDigits:`), which was written out several times before, now lives here once.

**`Identification`** (subclasses `DNI` and `CUIT`)
- `Identification type:number:` picks the subclass whose `typeCode` matches ('D' or 'C'). If none matches, it raises 'Invalid identification type'.
- Each subclass holds its own validation rules and error message.
- The base class answers `isDNI`, `isCUIT`, `dniNumberIfNone:` and `cuitNumberIfNone:` with the "none" case, and each subclass overrides only the method for its own type.

**`ZipCode`** (subclasses `OldZipCode` and `NewZipCode`)
- `ZipCode for:` picks the subclass with `canHandle:`: a string starting with a digit is old, one starting with a letter is new.
- A new zip code is valid when it has 8 characters, ends in 3 letters and its 4 middle characters form a valid old zip code. That removes the old repeated digit and "greater than 999" checks.
- `isOld`, `isNew`, `oldZipCodeIfNone:` and `newZipCodeIfNone:` work the same way as for `Identification`. `value` returns a number for an old zip code and a string for a new one, which is what the tests expect.

## Changes to existing classes
- **`CustomerImporter`:** `importCustomer` and `importAddress` are now a few lines each. They build the values with `Identification type: record fourth number: record fifth` and `ZipCode for: record fifth`.
- **`Customer`:** the `identificationType` and `identificationNumber` fields became a single `identification` field. The methods the tests call now just pass the question on to that object. I added `isIdentifiedAs:number:`.
- **`Address`:** it now holds a `ZipCode` object. The `isKindOf:` checks are gone.
- **`TransientCustomerSystem` and `PersistentCustomerSystem`:** both repeated the same "type and number match" check in `customerWithIdentificationType:number:`. Both now use `isIdentifiedAs:number:`.

## Things to know
- `ImportTest` was in `CustomerImporter-Recu-1er-Parcial`. As your instructions asked, I moved it to `CustomerImporter-Recu-1er-Parcial-Tests` without changing its code.
- Test 29 expects the message 'Invalid identification type' for a bad zip code, so `ZipCode` raises that same text.
- I left the check for record type ('C' or 'A') in `importRecord`, and the `isKindOf: Customer` check in `DataBaseSession`, which only simulates a database. Neither one is about the ID or zip code types.
